title: The Generic Software Capability Maturity Model
description: Hover the five ascending maturity levels to place an organizational behavior at the right step.
creator: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
Capability Maturity Model for Systems Thinking
chapter_title: Capability Maturity Model for Systems Thinking

educational.learningObjective: Given the five generic maturity-level names, the learner will place a described organizational behavior at the correct step in the ascending sequence.
prerequisites: Has worked in or observed an organization with repeated processes
learningOutcomes: Name the five generic maturity levels in order
Place a described behavior at the correct level
Explain why maturity levels cannot be skipped
educational.assessmentOpportunity: Describe an organizational behavior and ask learners to name its level and justify it against the level below.

pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Ordered recall with a spatial mnemonic
pedagogical.feedbackType: Level name and description on hover
misconceptionsAddressed: That maturity levels can be achieved out of order
That the highest level is a destination rather than an ongoing practice
discussionQuestions: What does it take to move from Repeatable to Defined?
Is Optimizing an end state or a permanent activity?
Can one part of an organization be at a different level than another?
